renderedEvidence.fullResolutionInspection: Inspected the supplied 1536 by 1024 PNG pixels.
renderedEvidence.compactPreviewInspection: Inspected a proportional 360 by 240 preview. The laptop remains legible, but the pixel cat becomes a small secondary detail while the unsupported speech bubbles remain conspicuous.

visibleAudit.laptop: PASS: one open laptop rests plausibly on the table; hinge, keyboard, screen plane, support and shadow are coherent.
visibleAudit.cat: PASS: one small passive pixel-art cat is inside the lower-right screen area. It is neither a real cat nor an anthropomorphic actor.
visibleAudit.peopleAnimalsLogos: PASS: no people, hands, real animals, branded marks or readable words are visible.
visibleAudit.requiredBlankChatBar: PASS: one compact blank bar appears inside the display.
visibleAudit.style: PARTIAL: cyan, coral, deep ink, paper ground, linework and print grain recall the bound editorial reference, though the dominant laptop reads closer to a rendered product shot than the reference's layered editorial illustration. This is not the rejection basis.

visibleDefects.observation: The screen contains two large speech-bubble controls plus two sticky-note cards marked with fabricated line and glyph-like detail. The contract allows only abstract nonlegible note shapes behind one compact blank chat bar and prohibits fake interface controls, labels and generated text-like content.

The two speech bubbles are dominant, unbound interface-like decoration. They compete with the single control bar and the passive optional-pet distinction instead of explaining it. Their presence recreates the extra-clutter problem that v2 was meant to remove.

The article and contract require the pet to be optional scenery beside one compact control. At preview size the most legible screen signal is a generic multi-message conversation, so the image no longer makes the pet-versus-control distinction cleanly enough.

disposition.requiredRepair: Re-render with only the laptop, one passive pixel cat inside a screen corner, one blank compact chat bar and background-only abstract nonlegible marks. Remove both speech bubbles and the sticky-note cards or reduce any abstract marks until they cannot read as notes, labels or interface controls. Preserve the plausible laptop geometry and passive in-screen pixel cat.

limitations: This is private rendered-art review only. It does not approve the article, canonical binding, responsive implementation, deployment or the account-specific product behaviour described in the article.
The review distinguishes pixel inspection and compact-preview inspection from a later browser placement review.
